parsed.basis: Saint Thomas Middle Island is a parish on Saint Kitts, where consensual adult same-sex conduct has been lawful since the 2022 Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court decision struck the relevant Offences Against the Person Act provisions. There is no local statute protecting against discrimination or harassment on grounds of gender identity, no statutory remedy for discrimination in employment, education or accommodation, and no procedure to change gender markers on locally issued documents; visitors rely on home documents. No same-sex union is recognised. LGBTQ+ organisations are permitted to register, but police are not considered a reliable route to protection for anti-trans harassment or assault. No region-specific information distinguishes this parish from the national picture, and no separate local entry, facility or custody regime is known.
